content.title: Why Trees Matter
content.description: Trees are one of the most important non-linear data structures used in databases, file systems, search engines, operating systems, and competitive programming.

content.content: Unlike arrays and linked lists that store data linearly, trees organize information hierarchically. This structure enables efficient searching, insertion, deletion, and hierarchical representation of data.

content.title: Real-World Examples
content.content: Folder structures, company hierarchies, website navigation menus, XML/HTML documents, and database indexing all use tree-like structures.
A Tree is a hierarchical data structure consisting of nodes connected by edges. The topmost node is called the Root, and every node may have child nodes.

content.definition: A non-linear hierarchical data structure consisting of nodes connected by edges.

items.question: Root Node
items.answer: The topmost node of the tree.

items.question: Parent Node
items.answer: A node that has one or more child nodes.

items.question: Child Node
items.answer: A node connected below another node.

items.question: Height
items.answer: Maximum number of edges from root to deepest leaf.

items.question: Depth
items.answer: Distance from root to a node.

content.content: A Binary Tree is a tree in which each node can have at most two children: a Left Child and a Right Child.

content.title: Key Property
content.description: Every node can have zero, one, or two children.

items.question: Full Binary Tree
items.answer: Every node has either 0 or 2 children.

items.question: Complete Binary Tree
items.answer: All levels are filled except possibly the last level.

items.question: Perfect Binary Tree
items.answer: All internal nodes have two children and all leaves are at the same level.

items.question: Balanced Binary Tree
items.answer: Height difference between subtrees remains small.

content.content: Traversal refers to visiting every node in a tree exactly once in a specific order.

content.title: Interview Essential
content.content: Tree traversal questions are among the most common interview problems.
Level Order Traversal visits nodes level by level using a Queue.
What is a Binary Search Tree (BST)?
A Binary Search Tree is a Binary Tree that follows a special ordering rule.

content.definition: All nodes in the left subtree are smaller than the root, and all nodes in the right subtree are greater than the root.

content.title: Important Observation
content.content: Inorder Traversal of a BST always produces elements in sorted order.
BST allows efficient searching by eliminating half of the remaining tree during each comparison.
Insertion follows the BST property and places the new node at the appropriate location.
Deletion is more complex because BST ordering must be preserved after removal.

items.question: Two Children
items.answer: Replace using Inorder Successor or Predecessor.

content.title: Interview Tip
content.content: Remember that Inorder Traversal of a BST always produces sorted output. This property appears in many coding interview questions.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Binary Trees and BSTs form the foundation for AVL Trees, Red-Black Trees, Heaps, Segment Trees, Tries, and many advanced data structures.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Binary Trees allow at most two children.
Inorder traversal of BST is sorted.
BST search is O(log n) on average.
BST insertion and deletion maintain ordering.
